title: Relative supported Cartier Kummer boundary specification
statement: For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], a closed immersion $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ with invertible Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], a natural number $N$ invertible on $T$, and a commutative ring $A$ killed by $N$, use the ordinary small etale module derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Use the actual finite twist $A_T(1)$ [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] and the integral generator, roots scalar map, and module-to-abelian class realization [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class]. Define the divisor section of $L=\mathcal I_D^\vee=\mathcal O_T(D)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] by transposing the ideal inclusion. Its open pullback uses the normalized tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], transported to the recorded frame-torsor interface [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor]. For $c\in\operatorname{Ext}^2_A(i_*A_D,A_T(1))$, define the predicate that $c$ is the supported Kummer boundary as follows. For the complementary open $W=T-D$, there are a frame $\tau$ of $L$ over $W$ equal to the divisor section, a short exact extension $0\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow a E\xrightarrow b i_*\mathbf Z_D\to0$, and an equivariant map from the frame torsor of $L$ to $E$ whose image is the fibre over the supported section one and which sends $\tau$ to zero. Equivariance means $f(g+p)=a(g)+f(p)$; the fibre equation is $b(f(p))=1|_U$ on every etale object $U$. Require the image of $c$ under exact scalar forgetting and precomposition with $i_*\mathbf Z_D\to i_*A_D$ to equal the Yoneda product of this extension class with the actual short exact Kummer extension [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], followed by the scalar map $\mu_N\to A_T(1)$. Also define the ordinary Kummer Chern class of $L$ in abelian degree-two cohomology and the canonical constant-sheaf closed exchange as the existing base-change mate followed by the constant inverse-image comparison.
